You can use perfect modals (modal + have + past participle) to talk about uncertainty in the past.
You use can't have + past participle to show that you are almost sure that something did not happen in the past. You use it talk about impossibilities.

For example:
She can't have forgotten to invite you - you are her best friend!
You can't have seen him at the movies - he is in the hospital.
People assume that I can't have always been interested in matchmaking.
This can't have been the first time you've done this.
The information they've given me can't have been invented or embellished.
You can use prepositions and a gerund after some verbs. There are certain patterns to keep in mind, depending on the verb and which preposition you use.

images.text:
Margaret Vanderkamp, the founder of Connect Dating Service (CDS), discourages people from referring to her as a matchmaker. "I think of myself as a connector," she says. "I just try to help people who find it a little difficult to meet that special someone."
Margaret says that she was always fascinated by what men and women find attractive about each other. "People assume that I can't have always been interested in matchmaking, but even in college, I could just tell when two friends were meant for each other," says Margaret. "I think I was born with a special gift to recognize that invisible chemistry that exists between men and women. It's something intuitive.”
Margaret says that most people have never heard of anyone owning a matchmaking business.

How does one begin a matchmaking service? they always ask. It can't have been easy. But Margaret explains that before she opened CDS in her basement, she had already introduced many of her friends and relatives to their present spouses. "People were always impressed with my knack for bringing people together," she says." 'This can't have been the first time you've done this,' they'd always say. Eventually I decided that if I was going to be doing it anyway, I might as well make some money from it."

Margaret says that the secret to matchmaking is listening to her clients' souls. "I have to concentrate when I'm interviewing a client. Truthfulness is important. The information they've given me can't have been invented or embellished," Margaret continues. "I insist on conducting the interviews myself, and I start by telling them that they need to communicate with me openly. Many tell me that they feel all alone in the world with no one to help them. I try to convince them that there's a solution to loneliness."
Margaret says that her most important message is that people should feel positive about their potential. "They must be filled with hope. They must be optimistic that they'll find someone with whom to share their lives."
